area: mac4DSTEM/App/AppState.swift — the @Observable facade (state consistency, gate derivation, error paths, concurrency)
summary: This file is far better disciplined than its line count suggests, and the report should be read against that. What it does WELL, verified by reading rather than by trusting comments: (1) the `datasetEpoch` + `operationController.isCurrent(token)` pair is applied consistently at every one of the ~14 detached publish sites and every late progress/status closure, so no result from a previous dataset or a superseded operation can land — this is the strongest thing in the file; (2) the S6 `AnalysisRunOutcome` is written at the exit site instead of scraped from `statusText`, and `runDPC` even withholds `.published` when the display derivation refuses (AppState.swift:4315-4318); (3) refusals are deliberately routed to DURABLE channels (`sessionSidecar.noteUnreadable`, `gates.noteSidecarRestoreFailed`) because `statusText` was measured to be overwritten — that lesson is applied at every site that learned it; (4) `activate` genuinely keeps the view/source distinction (the `sourceDescriptor` naming and `CalibrationReReference` step, AppState.swift:2390-2530); (5) the eight extracted seams really do have no forwarding properties, so the rule held. The findings below are five places where one policy still has two derivations, or where a cached value outlives the thing it describes. NOT re-reported because docs/open-items.md already carries them: `quantitativeStatus`'s fall-through to `.quantitative` (:735-746), the Q-calibration reference-shell selection (~:5038-5051), `?? .fullExtent` provenance fabrication (:2848), `applySessionCalibration` adopting a sidecar-frame calibration unchecked, and the three hand-rolled copies of the open/unwind tail. One thing I deliberately did NOT call a defect after checking it: `calibrateEllipse`'s `meanOrigin ?? geometric middle` (:4113) looks like the S11 class but is harmless, because it strips the ellipse first, which makes `BraggVectors.calibrated` return the raw peaks unchanged (DiskDetection.swift:421). SEAMS TO EXTRACT NEXT, ranked: (1) **result identity/provenance** — `restoredResult*`/`navigationResult*` (AppState.swift:257-270) plus `currentResult*` (ResultExport.swift:1685-1712): six untyped optional tuples with no owner, written at ~20 sites and cleared at ~18 of them by hand; finding 1 lives exactly there and a `ResultIdentity` value with one `publish()`/`clear()` closes it structurally rather than by vigilance. Smallest change, highest value, and it is the class this repo keeps getting burned by. (2) **the parallax/ptychography reconstruction workflow** — ~25 stored properties (:285-345) and 7 near-identical run functions (:3470-3960), already carrying an implicit invalidation graph in `didSet` cascades; it touches nothing outside `resultImage` publication and `datasetEpoch`, so it is the `StrainProduct` precedent applied to the biggest contiguous block in the file. (3) **ACOM** — `App/ACOMWorkflow.swift` already exists but holds only enums; finding 4 exists because the plan's inputs (model, quality, AND wavelength) have no single owner. (4) **display/contrast presentation** (~40 members plus four version-keyed caches) — pure derivation, testable with no dataset at all.

findings.title: restoredResultPixelInfo is never cleared, so a freshly computed product exports with the restored session map's pixel size, units and provenance
findings.why: `restoredResultInfo` and `restoredResultPixelInfo` are set together at exactly two sites (AppState.swift:2949-2953, :2961-2965, plus ResultExport.swift:839-843, :851-855) but only the FIRST is ever set back to nil — at ~18 sites (e.g. :789, :2562, :3938, :4741, :4939, :4970). `restoredResultPixelInfo` has no nil-assignment anywhere in the tree (verified by grep over mac4DSTEM/). The `resultImage`/`resultRGBA` didSet clears `navigationResultPixelInfo` and conditionally `restoredResultDomain` (:240-246, :248-254) but never the restored pixel info, and `activate` (:2562) clears the label triple without it, so the leak also crosses datasets. The consumer is asymmetric with the labels: `currentResultKind/DisplayName/ValueUnits` key on `restoredResultInfo` (ResultExport.swift:1685-1695) while `currentResultPersistenceMetadata` keys on `restoredResultPixelInfo` (ResultExport.swift:1699-1701). `saveCurrentResultToSessionSidecar` guards correctly (`if restoredResultInfo != nil`, ResultExport.swift:722-724) — proving the intended pairing — but the PNG/figure export path does not: ResultExport.swift:204-210 takes `pixel.row/column/units` from that stale tuple to draw the BURNED-IN SCALE BAR, and :232-240 writes `pixel.provenance` into the PNG metadata. `displayedProduct` (AppState.swift:681-688) also reads its `sampling`, `provenance` and `quantitativeStatus` from it. No test in mac4DSTEMTests/ or tools/ references either field.
findings.failureScenario: Open a dataset whose sidecar holds a saved ptychography-phase map (pixelSizeRow = object sampling in Å, units "A"). `restoreSessionResult` (:2946-2971) sets both restored tuples. The open's own automatic whole-cube pass (`runCurrentAnalysis` at :2316) then runs `runVirtualDetector`, which sets `restoredResultInfo = nil` (:3938) and publishes a new scan-domain image. The title and units now correctly say "Virtual detector" — but `currentResultPersistenceMetadata` still returns the ptychography map's row/column/units/provenance. Export the virtual-detector image as a publication PNG: the burned-in scale bar is drawn at the ptychography object sampling in Å instead of the scan pixel size, and the PNG metadata carries `source_product: ptychography_object_phase`. The same stale dictionary supplies `quantitative_status` to `displayedProduct`, so the new product inherits the old one's trust badge.

findings.title: Changing the accelerating voltage does not invalidate the cached orientation plan, so ACOM re-runs against a flat-Ewald template library and reports in-plane angle only modulo 180°
findings.why: `generateOrientationPlan` derives `planWavelength` from `acceleratingVoltage` (:5121-5124) and passes it into `OrientationPlan.generate`, where it selects the excitation-error model: `sg = g·n + (λ/2)|g|²` (OrientationPlan.swift:184-185). The repo's own documentation of that parameter (OrientationPlan.swift:153-161) states that without a wavelength the sphere is flat, every template is EXACTLY π-periodic in azimuth, and "the reported in-plane angle is only determined modulo 180°". `invalidateACOMPlan()` (:773-777) is triggered by `acomModelSelection` (:443), `acomQuality` (:460), `customZ` (:765), `customStructure` (:767) and `customLatticeA` (:770) — but NOT by `acceleratingVoltage`. `setManualAcceleratingVoltage` (:3211-3219), wired to a UI field at UI/ContentView.swift:512, only clears the parallax products and conditionally calls `invalidateACOMResult()` (the RESULT, not the PLAN). `runACOM` regenerates only when the plan is absent: `if orientationPlan == nil { await generateOrientationPlan() }` (:5168). So the plan silently survives the change to its own physics input.
findings.failureScenario: Open a file whose metadata carries no `accelerating_voltage` (`acceleratingVoltage` is set nil at :2477). Run ACOM: the plan is built with `wavelengthAngstrom: nil` — flat Ewald sphere, π-degenerate templates. Prepare's readiness then tells the user to supply the voltage (it is a listed requirement for quantitative work), so they type it into the inspector field. Re-run ACOM: `orientationPlan != nil`, so the flat-Ewald library is reused unchanged. The IPF·Z map, the In-plane angle map and the Euler φ₁/φ₂ maps are all published with 180° ambiguities the physical plan would have resolved, labelled with the physical-scale provenance from `acomScaleSemantics`, recorded into the replay recipe (:5240-5246) and exported. Nothing on screen distinguishes this from a correctly generated plan.

findings.title: Cancel during an open's first whole-cube pass stops nothing and its own message is immediately overwritten by advancing progress
findings.why: `beginDatasetLoading` creates `datasetLoadCancellation` (:2696) and that token is threaded into `buildDatasetPreview` (:2694) and `preloadResidentCube` (:2727) — both cancel correctly. But the final `await runCurrentAnalysis()` of an open (:2316 in `openFileAsync`, :1657 in `commitPendingLoad`, :1758 in `promoteToFullExtent`) enters `runVirtualDetector`, which mints its OWN token from `beginCancellableOperation` (:3390) and hands only that one to `VirtualDetector.tiledRun`. `cancelDatasetLoad()` (:1206-1213) cancels only `datasetLoadCancellation`; it never calls `operationController.cancelCurrent()`. Worse, the still-live analysis keeps writing over the cancellation notice: `updateCancellableOperation` is guarded on `!token.isCancelled` for the ANALYSIS token (:1263) and then does `if isLoadingDataset { datasetLoadingProgress = progress; datasetLoadingStatus = status }` (:1265-1268) — neither it nor `reportDatasetLoadingProgress` (:2775) consults `isCancellingDatasetLoad`. Meanwhile `canCancelDatasetLoad` (:1201-1203) has gone false, so the button disappears. The welcome card is explicitly still on screen during this phase (`openFileAsync`'s own comment at :2310-2315) and its Cancel is the only one rendered there (UI/ProductWorkspaceViews.swift:191-195). docs/open-items.md records two other hazards of this tail and that F1.1d ("cancel a real load on screen") has never been driven; it does not record this one.
findings.failureScenario: Open a 17 GB DM4 by mistake — the exact scenario the Cancel affordance was built for. Metadata read, preview and preload all pass. The whole-cube virtual-detector pass starts and the card shows "Scanning patterns 1,378 / 16,218 · 3.96 GB of 46.6 GB". Press Cancel: `isCancellingDatasetLoad` goes true, the button vanishes, "Cancelling…" appears for one frame and is then replaced by the next progress tick, and the counter keeps climbing to 16,218 while the entire cube is read. Only after the pass finishes does :2318 observe `datasetLoadWasCancelled` and discard. The user sees a Cancel that was visibly ignored, with no way to press it again.

findings.title: The cached CoM field is not invalidated when the origin it was measured against changes, so a later DPC display switch renders it under the new origin's provenance
findings.why: `comField` (:348) caches the measured centre-of-mass field so display switches are instant (:4308). Its defining input is the origin `computeCoMField` subtracts (:4222-4227: `calibration.origin?.interleavedFitted` plus `calibration.referenceOrigin(...)`). Two functions change exactly that input and clear the OTHER origin-dependent caches beside it while leaving `comField` untouched: `updateAperture` moves the fitted maps to `supersededFittedOrigin`, sets `calibration.origin = nil`, clears `recordedOriginX/Y` and stamps `.manual`, then clears `parallaxPreprocess`/`parallaxAlignment` (:3102-3121) — but not `comField`; `restoreFittedOrigin` reinstates the maps and again clears only the parallax pair (:3086-3096). The asymmetry inside one function is the evidence this is an oversight, not a decision. `comField` is nil-ed only in `activate` (:2579). `applyDPCDisplay` (:4378) re-renders straight from the cache on any `dpcDisplay` change (:997-999), and the export provenance is read from LIVE calibration state at export time (ResultExport.swift:1478-1522), so the two can describe different origins.
findings.failureScenario: In Virtual Detector mode drag the aperture centre (fitted origin superseded, provenance `.manual`). Switch to DPC and run it — `comField` is now measured against the manual centre, with no per-position origins subtracted. Go to Prepare and press Restore Fitted Origin (:3086): the maps come back, `hasFittedOrigin` is true again, `comField` is untouched. Back in DPC, change the display to iDPC: `applyDPCDisplay` renders from the stale cache, and because `idpcPhysicalCalibration` (:4436-4452) now passes (fitted origin + rotation + gate), the image is rendered as PHYSICAL iDPC in radians. Exporting it writes `"quantitative": "true"` and `"origins_subtracted": "fitted_per_position"` (ResultExport.swift:1478-1495) for a field whose per-position origins were never subtracted.

findings.title: The strain and ACOM fit-verification overlays are anchored on a fifth hand-rolled origin fallback, so they are drawn at a different point than the analysis they verify
findings.why: `overlayReferenceOrigin` is `calibration.meanOrigin ?? (x: qx/2, y: qy/2)` (:5310-5313) and feeds both `strainFitOverlay` (:5333) and `acomFitOverlay` (:5350). The analyses those overlays verify use `calibratedBraggVectors` (:4747-4755), which S13 rewrote to call `Calibration.referenceOrigin` — the function whose doc comment states it is "**The one derivation of 'which origin do I re-centre on?'**" and that "A new caller belongs here, not in a fifth hand-rolled `?? (qx/2, qy/2)`" (Core/Data/Calibration.swift:652-659). The two disagree in every state where `calibration.origin` is nil but a beam centre is known: `referenceOrigin` returns `.recordedMean` (Calibration.swift:664-666) or `.apertureCentre` (:667-669), while the overlay falls to the geometric middle. `FitOverlays.localOrigin` falls back to the passed `referenceOrigin` under exactly the same map-usability rule (Core/Analysis/FitOverlays.swift:66-79), so the displacement is not absorbed downstream. The magnitude of this exact substitution is already measured in this repo: 1.14 px on `sim_Au` and 7.07 px on `downsample_Si_SiGe_exp` (S13 E1, quoted in Calibration.swift:598-601).
findings.failureScenario: Open a py4DSTEM bundle carrying `qx0_mean`/`qy0_mean` with no per-position origin maps — the ordinary shape of a calibration bundle, per Calibration.swift:626-628. `activate` stores it as `recordedOriginX/Y` with provenance `.fileMean` (:2497-2503), leaving `calibration.origin` nil. Run disk detection then strain: the map is computed about the recorded beam centre (`referenceOrigin` kind `.recordedMean`). Turn on the fit overlay and inspect a position: `overlayReferenceOrigin` returns the detector's geometric middle instead, so the reference and local lattice vectors are drawn from a point 7.07 px off on that dataset, systematically offset from the stored raw peaks (`storedPeaksAtSelection`, :5318) they are meant to be judged against. The user reads a correct fit as a bad one — or accepts a bad one — from the instrument built to make that judgement.
